display: Berlin-based label runner and live-sound engineer: a vinyl-only experimental label (drone, folk instruments, modular synths) with fourteen releases, mastered in-house.

signals.text: I'm looking for an East Asian free-reed player (sheng, khaen or shō) who works seriously with electronics, for a spring compilation.
My compilation has plenty of breathing instruments already. I want contrast, something that bites, so the record doesn't turn into soup.
The compilation is eight tracks on two LPs. Accordion and harmonium artists are signed, and one slot is still open.
I need artists' files by early January to hit a spring release.
I'm mastering a drone record by a Leipzig cellist this month, and the files go to the pressing plant on 25 October.
Pressing costs keep rising, and I'm weighing whether some releases should go to cassette. I love vinyl and I'm torn.
I'm tired of audiences who talk through quiet music. I want to find the people who actually listen.
My modular crashed in the middle of a long patch and there was no recall. I'm looking for a reliable way to save and recall patches.
I co-host a Sunday community radio show and I'm looking for guests and music with rhythm that still fits an experimental show.
I'm hunting for a flat in Berlin, probably Wedding or Moabit, close to the U8, before January.
My basement studio gets damp every autumn. I want practical ways to protect records and gear, and the landlord isn't helping.
I'm unsure whether I'll be able to keep the basement studio long-term.
I'm trying to cook Georgian food (khachapuri) and want advice on getting the egg yolk right.

offers.text: In-house mastering for vinyl, including lathe-cut test pressings, plus a small listening room for critical review.
A Neukölln basement studio with a modular synth rack, available for recording sessions and visits by arrangement.
Working relationships with two pressing plants, one in the Czech Republic and one in Germany, and practical knowledge of small runs of 300 to 500.
Distribution through three European shops and a mailing list of about 2,300 listeners of experimental music.
Booking contacts in Berlin, Rotterdam, Ghent and Lyon for small, attentive-audience shows.
Years of festival live-sound experience, available for freelance engineering of live and quiet-music events.
A regular volunteer slot on a Sunday community radio show, where I can air music from artists I work with.
Curation and sequencing for compilations and albums, including editing long pieces to fit the sides of a record.

catchers.hypo: I play the sheng (or khaen, or shō) and I've been layering it with modular synths. I've never been on a record. Are you interested?
catchers.can: Listen to the material and, if it fits, offer a slot on the spring free-reed compilation (vinyl, two LPs), with a modest advance and mastering done in-house.
catchers.confirm: Do you play a free-reed mouth organ (sheng, khaen, shō or similar) and have you recorded it with electronics?

catchers.hypo: I know a sheng player in Taipei or Shanghai who does experimental work and would love a European release. Can I introduce them?
catchers.can: Take the intro, listen, and consider them for the compilation's open slot.
catchers.confirm: Is the player you're recommending someone who has recorded or performed with electronics, not only traditional repertoire?

catchers.hypo: I've made a long drone or acoustic-instrument record and I need it mastered for vinyl. Can you help?
catchers.can: Master the record for lathe cut or plant pressing, and advise on sequencing and side length.
catchers.confirm: Is your record meant for vinyl and finished in a mix, with stems or a stereo file ready?

catchers.hypo: I run a small label and I'm trying to decide between pressing vinyl or cassette for a 300-copy run. What would you do?
catchers.can: Share what I've learned about pressing plants and quotes, and connect them to Camille, who runs a sister label in Lyon and recently moved to cassette.
catchers.confirm: Is this a run of under 1,000 copies of experimental or niche music?

catchers.hypo: I want to put out a small cassette-only batch and need a duplicator and a printing contact in Europe.
catchers.can: Ask Camille in Lyon for her cassette supplier and unit costs, then pass along what she's willing to share.
catchers.confirm: Is your run a small edition of cassettes, rather than a mass-market product?

catchers.hypo: I'm an accordion or harmonium player and I'd like to combine acoustic reeds with electronics.
catchers.can: Introduce them to Pieter, the Rotterdam accordionist on the compilation, who works with separable drone stems, and to the Ghent harmonium duo.
catchers.confirm: Do you play an acoustic reed instrument and want to work with synths or drones?

catchers.hypo: I run a supper club or small venue and want a quiet-listening evening with live sound and food from different cuisines.
catchers.can: Offer live-sound engineering and curation, and connect them to my housemate Mara, a chef, if they need Georgian or other home-style cooking.
catchers.confirm: Is your event small and meant for attentive listening, with a sound set-up you can adjust?

catchers.hypo: I run a venue or a series with a quiet-listening policy and I'd love advice on how to keep audiences from talking during soft sets.
catchers.can: Talk through my experience as a festival sound engineer and a label runner, and book acts suited to listening rooms.
catchers.confirm: Do you run a room or series where quiet, attentive listening is the main aim?

catchers.hypo: My modular patch crashed with no recall. I'm trying to build a workflow where I never lose a long patch again.
catchers.can: Share the habits I'm adopting to document patches, and compare notes on hardware or software that helps.
catchers.confirm: Do you work with a hardware modular rig, rather than a software-only setup?

catchers.hypo: I have a damp cellar studio or record storage. What actually works against moisture in autumn?
catchers.can: Share what I've tried, including raised shelving and dehumidifiers, and talk through what has and hasn't worked.
catchers.confirm: Is your problem damp in a basement or cellar space used for records or equipment?

catchers.hypo: I'm an artist whose work is niche and quiet, and I'm doubting whether it can ever be a real career. Does anyone get this?
catchers.can: Talk honestly about running a small label from the experimental side for six years, with its rewards and its limits.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for a peer conversation about sustaining niche creative work, rather than business consulting?

forbids.text: I only release on vinyl in small pressings, and I don't do streaming-first releases.
I can't pay artist advances above a modest level, so projects needing larger fees won't fit.
For a spring release I need artists' files by early January, so I can't take on timelines that run later.
I'm Berlin-based and most work happens in person or by post, so I can't travel for long periods.
I won't release music I haven't listened to closely myself, and I don't take on projects as an anonymous pressing service.

projects.name: Spring compilation: free-reed instruments + modular synths
projects.text: Two LPs, eight tracks, vinyl-only, for next spring. Accordion (Rotterdam) and harmonium duo (Ghent) are signed. Still missing an East Asian free-reed player to add contrast.
roles_needed: East Asian free-reed player (sheng, khaen or shō) who works with electronics
Writer or radio host to help present the record

policy.t1: When there's a real lead, I'll share the compilation plans, which instrument is missing, the rough advance range, the timeline, and introductions to artists and label contacts.
policy.t2: Once trust is established, I'll talk about my studio situation, the housing worries, and the practical constraints of running the label.
policy.never: I won't share family details or any money details, including my finances and the label's accounts.
